title: IB English Literature Exam Technique for November
summary: IB English Literature exam technique for November, with current Paper 1 and Paper 2 structures, timing plans, marking criteria and practical tips.
body_markdown:
Three weeks before the November session, an IB English Literature student does not need another folder of quotations. They need control: control of the clock, the question and the line of argument.


Effective **IB English Literature exam technique** means understanding exactly what each paper asks, planning before writing and connecting every literary choice to an interpretation. For the November 2026 session, the current Language A: Literature guide, first assessed in 2026, gives SL and HL students the same core challenge: produce focused literary analysis under time pressure. HL students complete more analysis in Paper 1, while Paper 2 follows the same format at both levels.


The November session does not create a separate paper structure or marking system. Your level determines the format. Confirm your personal timetable and local starting times with your coordinator.


### Your three-week exam checklist


When Paper 1 priority Paper 2 priority


Three weeks to go Practise identifying a passage's central tension and important authorial choices Build comparison maps for your strongest pairs of works


Two weeks to go Write complete analyses within the correct SL or HL time Plan several questions, then write complete comparative essays


Final week Complete timed practice and review recurring weaknesses Rehearse flexible evidence rather than memorising one essay


Day before Review your timing routine and analytical vocabulary Review work pairings, turning points and precise references


The goal is not to predict the question. It is to make your response process dependable. RevisionDojo's comparison of[IB English Paper 1 and Paper 2](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/is-ib-english-paper-2-harder-than-paper-1-a-comparative-guide) can help you decide where your remaining time will have the greatest effect.


### Three weeks out: understand Paper 1


Paper 1 is a guided literary analysis of unseen writing. The passages may be complete works or extracts, and each has a guiding question focused on a technical or formal feature.


At SL, you receive two unseen literary passages from different literary forms. You choose one and have 1 hour 15 minutes to produce one analysis worth 20 marks. At HL, you analyse both passages separately in 2 hours 15 minutes. Each response is worth 20 marks, giving 40 marks overall. Paper 1 contributes 35% of the final subject result at both levels.


Criterion What earns marks Maximum per response


A: Understanding and interpretation A convincing reading supported by relevant passage references 5


B: Analysis and evaluation Explanation of how authorial choices create meaning 5


C: Focus and organisation A sustained argument with purposeful development 5


D: Language Clear, precise and appropriately formal expression 5


The guiding question is an entry point, not a list of devices to find. Before writing, complete this sentence: *The writer uses X to reveal, complicate or challenge Y.* That becomes the provisional argument.


For prose, consider narrative perspective, syntax, imagery, characterization and shifts in pace. For poetry, examine voice, structure, sound, lineation and patterns of imagery. For drama, remember that stage directions, entrances, pauses and spatial relationships are choices intended for performance.


A strong paragraph follows a causal chain:


**Choice → immediate effect → larger pattern → interpretation**


Do not stop at “the metaphor creates imagery.” Explain what the metaphor makes the reader notice, how it develops across the passage and why that pattern matters. Use the[Paper 1 sample essay questions](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/sample-essay-questions-for-ib-english-literature-paper-1) to practise turning guiding questions into arguable claims.


### A workable Paper 1 timing plan


SL students can spend roughly 10 minutes reading and planning, 60 minutes writing and 5 minutes checking. HL students might use 15 minutes to read and outline both responses, around 55 minutes on each analysis and 10 minutes for final checks. These are practice models, not IB rules. Adjust them only after timed work shows what you can sustain.


A student completes timed practice while inspiration waits outside the door


The comic contains an uncomfortable truth. Inspiration is welcome, but it cannot be your timing strategy.


### Two weeks out: make Paper 2 genuinely comparative


Paper 2 is a comparative essay completed in 1 hour 45 minutes. You choose one of four general questions and compare two literary works studied during the course. The paper is worth 25 marks. It contributes 35% at SL and 25% at HL.


Under the current guide, marks are distributed across five areas:


Criterion Focus Marks


A Knowledge, understanding and interpretation of the works 5


B1 Analysis and evaluation of authorial choices 5


B2 Comparison and contrast of authorial choices 5


C Focus, organisation and development 5


D Language 5


B2 is why two separate mini-essays are costly. Comparison must shape the argument, not appear in a sentence added at the end of each paragraph. The[IB English Paper 2 structure guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/understanding-the-ib-english-a-literature-paper-2-exam-structure-or-language-and-literature-guide) provides a fuller breakdown of this demand.


Choose the question for which you can discuss both works through authorial decisions. Then create a two-column plan containing three comparative claims. A useful paragraph structure is:


1. State one claim answering the question.
2. Analyse a precise moment from the first work.
3. Pivot to the second work using similarity or contrast.
4. Analyse why the second author handles the idea differently.
5. Explain what the comparison reveals.


Prepare references to scenes, structural turns, relationships, motifs and endings. You will write without the works in front of you, but accuracy matters more than a large collection of brittle, half-remembered quotations. A precise account of a moment can support analysis when exact wording is uncertain.


Use about 10 minutes to choose the question, 15 minutes to plan, 70 minutes to write and 10 minutes to revise. If selection is slow, practise choosing among prompts using the strategies in[Paper 2 under time pressure](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-to-prepare-for-the-ib-english-paper-2-exam-under-time-pressure-or-revisiondojo-strategies) .


### The final week: practise decisions, not scripts


In the last week, the student's temptation is to memorise one elegant essay. That feels safe because it removes uncertainty. It is also dangerous because the examination question may demand a different emphasis.


Instead, build flexible knowledge. For each work, prepare a one-page map covering narrative or dramatic structure, central tensions, recurring images, significant relationships, beginning, climax and ending. Then connect two works around adaptable lenses such as power, identity, conflict, memory, setting and transformation.


RevisionDojo can bring this practice into one workflow. Use the[IB English Paper 1 Questionbank](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib/ib-english-langlit-new/ib-english-langlit-new-2-paper-1/questionbank) to drill unseen analysis skills, while recognising that Literature passages are literary rather than non-literary. Study Notes and Flashcards can reinforce terminology and textual evidence. AI Chat can challenge a thesis, while grading tools can expose where commentary has become descriptive.


Most importantly, practise in the **Questionbank** and sit timed papers in **Exam mode** . After each attempt, record one issue under argument, evidence, analysis, comparison, organisation or language. The next session should target that issue. This is more useful than simply completing another essay and hoping repetition will solve everything.


### On the morning of the November exam


Read the command and focus of the question before searching for techniques. Plan a thesis that answers the whole task. Leave enough time to develop the final analytical paragraph rather than sacrificing it to an oversized introduction.


Then write with one principle in mind: literary features earn their value through interpretation. A symbol, pause or narrative shift is not impressive because it has a name. It matters because of what it allows the work to suggest.


Three weeks earlier, the student may have wanted certainty. By exam morning, something better is possible: a repeatable method. RevisionDojo's Questionbank, Exam mode, Mock Exams, Predicted Papers, Study Notes, Coursework Library and Tutors can support that method, but the final aim is simple. See the choice, explain its effect and keep answering the question.
